correctness.rationale: Proof independently checked all n>=3: continuants are irreducible primitive linear polynomials in an endpoint diagonal; adjugate diagonal cofactors exclude rank n-1 singularities; decomposing at zero bridges gives at most one kernel direction per irreducible chain and corank>=2 iff a Y_j condition holds. The three disjoint-variable equations form a prime regular sequence; a witness with all other bridges nonzero separates components. Determinant expansion F=UV-C b_j^2, invertible endpoint-diagonal Jacobian where C!=0, and nonzero rational witnesses give genuine transverse ordinary quadratic nodes. Codimension-two singular support and hypersurface CM yield R1/S2 normality. The packaged exact code was executed from its actual path; finite grid results are supplementary and not universal certification.

originality.rationale: The surviving claim is the complete n-1 component decomposition for the special variable-bridge tridiagonal linear section, individual j(n-j) component degrees and exact generic nodal coordinates. Piontkowski Proposition 1.5 covers the ambient corank-two degree binomial(n+1,3) and nodal behavior for general symmetric sections; these known facts are excluded as stand-alone novelty. Kerner--Vinnikov treats broad symmetric matrix representations without the sparse path decomposition; Henrion--Naldi--Safey El Din treats real algorithms under generic hypotheses. Relevant fixed-bridge continuants have no zero-bridge singular strata. No inspected primary source or exact-index search was found to imply the joint family-specific statement, subject to residual unindexed-source risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed older literature on Jacobi/continuant matrices or sparse symmetric degeneracy loci could explicitly state the same decomposition.
Piontkowski general degree formula already covers the aggregate numerical degree; its proof does not itself provide the componentwise geometry.
Huang thesis and historical sparse-matrix literature were not inspected exhaustively.

value.rationale: The family is the canonical variable symmetric band-one determinantal variety. A complete irreducible-component stratification with intrinsic equations and degrees, plus uniform generic local type, is a natural and structural singularity classification for every n. The generic full-symmetric corank-two degree does not characterize this nongeneric sparse section, so the new family-specific component geometry has independent mathematical utility. Limitations: no special-intersection singularities or global Jacobian primary decomposition.
